idea: Replace the random shuffle with a target-similarity filter plus dedup. Steps: (1) Fit a TfidfVectorizer on character n-grams (analyzer='char_wb', ngram_range=(2,4), sublinear_tf=True, max_features=200000, on the first 3000 chars of each doc) over pool + target_sample; also build a word-level TF-IDF (1-2 grams, min_df=2). (2) Train a LogisticRegression (C=1, class_weight='balanced') with the 200 target_sample docs as positives and a seeded random sample of 3000 pool docs as negatives on the hstacked features; score every pool doc with decision_function. (3) Drop exact and near duplicates: keep the first occurrence by hash of the whitespace-normalised, lowercased first 500 characters. (4) Drop junk: docs under 200 characters, docs whose unique-word ratio is below 0.2, or whose fraction of alphabetic+space characters is below 0.7. (5) Count tokens with tiktoken gpt2 (encode_ordinary_batch) and rank surviving docs by classifier score descending; take top-scored docs until the cumulative token count reaches 1.0*T (if the clearly-positive set, score > 0, holds fewer than T tokens, still fill up to T with the next best-scored docs rather than cycling). (6) Shuffle the selected indices with random.Random(CURATE_SEED) so the training order is mixed, and return that list.
why: The pool is ~2T tokens with large amounts of spam, forum/Q&A and news text, so spending the fixed T-token budget only on deduplicated documents that most resemble the WikiText-style target (with its distinctive '= Title =' and ' @-@ ' tokenisation) should cut domain mismatch and wasted steps far more than any ordering trick.
outcome: dev 1.9322 against 1.9644 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best
